issues.title: Add a distributions layer to the study snapshot contract
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- Add an optional `distributions` array to the study snapshot schema, with #617's columns: `GroupID`, `GroupLevel`, `Source` (`Numerator` | `Denominator`), `Variable`, `Category`, `Count`, `Participants`, `Total`, `Percent`, plus `MetricID`, `SnapshotDate` and `StudyID`.
- A blank category is represented as `null` and displayed as "Not recorded".
- Keep `details` until its consumer is replaced (#10), then remove it.

**Out:**
- Computing distributions (pipeline, gsm.roadmap#617).
- Rendering them (#10).

criteria.text: The schema accepts a valid `distributions` array. It rejects missing required columns, a `Source` outside `Numerator`/`Denominator`, negative counts, and a `Percent` outside 0–1.
A study file without `distributions` stays valid, because metrics without distributions are unaffected.
Contract tests cover the valid, invalid and empty cases.

issues.title: Generate simulated distributions for the #617 metrics

criteria.text: On the fixture, for numerator distributions, `Total` equals the metric's Numerator (per metric × group). This is a gsm.roadmap#617 acceptance check.
On the fixture, for denominator distributions, `Total` equals the metric's Denominator. This is a gsm.roadmap#617 acceptance check.
On the fixture, for single-value variables, the sum of `Count` over categories equals `Total`. This is a gsm.roadmap#617 acceptance check.
In each study's latest snapshot, every site in `results` for a configured metric has distribution rows.
The generated files validate against the #8 schema.

issues.title: Build a Layout A bar-chart distribution widget
issues.scopeSection:
**In:** a Layout A bar-chart widget following the contract in the gsm.roadmap#617 pipeline design.
- **Header:** metric name, percent, and numerator / denominator.
- **Scope of data:** filter to one metric and, optionally, one group. Site rows are summed to study level in one function; nothing else is derived.
- **Sections:** one per `Source` × `Variable`, numerator first.
- **Bars:** Σ `Count` per category, sorted by descending count, with "Not recorded" last. A top-N setting collapses the rest into a "+ k more" bar.
- **Two percentages per category, by default:**
  - the share of the metric's population: Σ `Count` / Σ `Total` (e.g. % of participants who discontinued);
  - the share of enrolled participants: Σ `Count` / the metric's Denominator, where the denominator is the enrolled population.
- **Labels:** business terms from configuration (e.g. "% Discontinued", "% Enrolled"). Never show "Numerator" or "Denominator". Tooltips may carry the longer context.
- **No duplicate total:** no total row when the header already shows that value.
- **Colours:** status categories take colours from a configurable status-to-colour map, and fall back to a neutral colour when no map is given. Reason categories aren't coloured.
- **Footnotes:** shown automatically when Σ `Count` > `Total` (multi-value variables, where a participant counts in several categories) and when "Not recorded" is present.
- **States:** empty (configured, but no rows) and missing (the metric has no distributions).
- **Accessibility:** accessible labels.
- **Replaces:** `breakdown-bar`, and removes the `details` consumer.

**Out:**
- The contents of the status-to-colour map (a separate issue).
- Other chart types.
- Pipeline computation.

criteria.text: The widget renders from the #9 fixture for every configured metric.
Displayed counts and both percentages equal independently summed fixture values (test).
The site-to-study summing sits in one tested function, so it can be qualified as dashboard logic (gsm.roadmap#625).
No user-facing text contains "Numerator" or "Denominator" (test).
There's no total row that repeats the header value.
Status colours come from configuration, and the neutral fallback applies when none are given (test).
Sorting, top-N collapsing, "Not recorded" placement, the footnotes, and the empty and missing states are tested.
A reviewer compares the rendered widget with the Layout A design and accepts it (visual comparison).

issues.title: Hide site-flag views on the study view by default
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- The default study view shows no site-flag counts:
  - the default tile has no flag bar;
  - `flag-dist` and `bar-outliers` are not in the default views.
- Configuration can re-enable them per study or per metric.

**Out:** the portfolio view.

criteria.text: A test asserts that the default study view renders no site-flag counts.
Enabling them through configuration restores them (test).
The portfolio view is unchanged.
A reviewer compares the default study view with the default described in Scope and accepts it (visual comparison).

issues.title: Fail visibly on unknown widget or metric references
issues.scopeSection:
**In:** each of these renders a visible placeholder naming the reference and the reason, and logs a warning:
- an unknown widget name;
- an unknown metric ID;
- a widget that doesn't apply to the metric's kind (for example a distribution widget on a metric without distributions).

There is no silent fallback.

**Applicability.** Every tile and chart widget applies to any site-level metric. `distribution-bar` applies only to a metric with a breakdown configuration, and `link-out` only to a metric with a configured report link. Using either on another metric is an incompatible reference: a placeholder names the widget, the metric and the reason, and a warning is logged. A configured metric with no rows, including an earlier snapshot whose breakdowns aren't published, keeps the empty states from #10.

**Unknown metric IDs** in configuration (breakdowns, report links, per-study views) are listed in a notice at the top of the study page, naming each reference and where it was found.

**Out:** validating configuration before rendering (a separate issue, to follow).

criteria.text: Tests cover each case, and the placeholder text names the bad reference.
Valid references render exactly as before.

issues.title: Configure detailed-report links per widget
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- A per-metric (or per-widget) link to its detailed report, taken from configuration.
- Relative paths, resolved against a configurable base, so links work wherever the reports are hosted.
- No link at all when none is configured, rather than a broken one.

**Out:** choosing the real destinations, which depends on where reports are deployed (gsm.roadmap#625, open question 4).

criteria.text: Links render from configuration for each configured metric.
Relative links resolve against the configured base (test).
An unconfigured metric renders no link.

issues.title: Reject portfolio inputs from mixed snapshot cycles
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- The portfolio input declares its cycle: a snapshot date or cycle ID in the manifest.
- Studies whose latest snapshot doesn't match the cycle are excluded from the current-cycle table and totals, and named in a visible notice.
- Missing studies are named too.
- Trend history is unaffected.

**Out:** how the pipeline signals that a cycle is complete (gsm.roadmap#624, open question 4).

criteria.text: With a fixture that has one study off-cycle, that study is excluded and named.
With a fixture that has one study off-cycle, totals equal the sum over the in-cycle studies.
With a fixture where every study is in cycle, the portfolio renders as before.

issues.title: Read the portfolio from a counts-only summary
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- The portfolio view reads one summary document:
  - each study's latest parameters;
  - per study × metric × snapshot: summed Numerator and Denominator, the site count, and flag counts.
- The summary holds counts only, with no stored rates.
- Rates and shares are computed after summing. A JSON Schema rejects stored ratios.
- The example-data generator writes the summary. In production, the portfolio repository produces it (gsm.roadmap#624, P1–P2).

**Out:** the production summary job.

criteria.text: A double-programming test shows that every portfolio number computed from the summary equals the number from pooling the per-study files.
The schema rejects ratios and unknown fields.
On the generated example data, `summary.json` is at most 10% of the combined size of all per-study snapshot files listed in the manifest, measured in bytes on disk without compression.

issues.title: Move portfolio defaults into a configuration file
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- Read `groupBy`, `heatmap`, `ramp`, `show` and the default visible metric columns from a configuration file. It's JSON for the prototype; #624 places the production defaults in the portfolio repository's YAML.
- Values are validated against the same vocabulary as the sidebar.

**Out:** the production configuration location.

criteria.text: Changing the configuration changes the initial view.
An invalid value fails with an actionable message (test).

issues.title: Add an eligibility-over-time widget
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- A time-series widget that plots the study-level `qtl0001` result (percent, with n/N) against snapshot date.
- Built on the gsm.viz `timeSeries` module, so it matches the standard report's chart.
- An empty state for a study with a single snapshot.

**Out:**
- Making past snapshots available to the render step. That's a deployment dependency: it needs read access to the snapshot history.
- Any new eligibility calculation.

criteria.text: The plotted values equal the study-level `qtl0001` results at each snapshot (test).
The axis, labels and markers match the standard eligibility report's chart (visual comparison).
The single-snapshot and missing-metric states are tested.

issues.title: Add status colours to distribution widgets
issues.scopeSection:
**In:** a status-to-colour map in configuration, with these entries.

| Group | Status | Colour |
|---|---|---|
| Eligibility | Eligible | teal |
| Eligibility | Ineligible | red |
| Eligibility | Potentially Ineligible | TBD |
| IP status | Dosed – ongoing; Dosed – treatment complete; Dosed – premature treatment discontinuation; Potential Non-Starter – within window; Potential Non-Starter – outside window; Confirmed Non-Starter | match the standard IP compliance report (palette TBD) |
| Study disposition (enrolled) | Withdrawal by Participant | red |
| Study disposition (enrolled) | Lost to Follow-Up | purple |
| Study disposition (enrolled) | Death | black |
| Study disposition (enrolled) | Ongoing | green |
| Study disposition (enrolled) | Study Discontinuation: Other; Study Completion | match the standard retention report (TBD) |
| Screening (all participants) | Screen Failure; In Screening; Enrolled | TBD |

- Colour names become the exact values used by the standard eligibility and retention reports.
- Unknown statuses fall back to the neutral colour and are reported.

**Out:**
- The colour hook in the widget (#10).
- Colours for reason categories.

criteria.text: Each listed status renders in its configured colour (test).
A status missing from the map uses the neutral colour and logs a warning (test).
The colours match the standard reports (visual comparison).

issues.title: Show the top protocol-deviation categories
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- Configure #10's widget: top 5 categories by count, counts only (percentages switched off), with ties broken alphabetically.
- One instance for important PDs.
- An optional second instance for non-important PDs, using configuration only.

**Out:**
- A new widget type.
- Harmonising categories across studies.

criteria.text: The top 5 categories and their counts equal independently summed fixture rows (test).
No percentages are shown.
The non-important variant renders from configuration alone.

issues.title: Move portfolio details into hovers and trim the tooltips
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- Remove the ⓘ icons.
- Show the metric definition on header hover, and study details, including the snapshot date, on study-name hover.
- Drop the Snapshot column.
- Remove the metric ID, Score and Threshold rows from the tooltip.
- Phrase rates per 28 days throughout, and use each metric's own denominator label (FB-019).

criteria.text: No ⓘ elements remain (test).
The header and study-name hovers show the moved content (test).
The tooltips contain no metric ID, score or thresholds.
A reviewer compares the hovers and tooltips with the design and accepts them (visual comparison).

issues.title: Add column options and a density toggle to the portfolio table
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- A column chooser: study name (default on), enrolled (default off), status (default off).
- Enrolled shown as n / expected when the data carries an enrollment target.
- A roomy/condensed toggle.
- Defaults read from the portfolio configuration (#16).

**Out:** adding the enrollment target to the data contract (a separate data change).

criteria.text: Each column toggles, and the defaults apply (tests).
n / expected renders when a target exists, and the count alone renders when it doesn't (tests).
The density toggle changes row spacing (visual check).

issues.title: Add a study filter and a full Reset to the portfolio
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- A multi-select study filter.
- A Reset button that restores every default: filters, metrics, heatmap, group-by and highlight.

criteria.text: The study filter limits the rows to the selected studies (test).
Reset restores the configured defaults (test).
A reviewer compares the study filter and Reset with the design and accepts them (visual comparison).

issues.title: Simplify heatmap options and fix shading under Group By
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- One colour ramp.
- The heatmap setting persists across filter changes, is cleared by Reset, and is kept in the URL.
- Expanded study rows are shaded.

criteria.text: Tests cover persistence across filters, clearing by Reset, and URL round-trips.
Expanded rows carry and display heat shading (test and visual check).

issues.title: Update the portfolio header
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- Add the RBQM logo.
- Remove the metadata line.
- Keep or remove the theme control, per the decision below.

criteria.text: The logo renders, and the metadata line is gone (visual check).

issues.title: Open the detailed report from a study and metric cell
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- A cell click opens the configured detailed report for that study and metric in a new tab, reusing the per-metric link configuration from #13.
- When no report is configured, there's no link, so nothing breaks.

criteria.text: Configured cells link to the right report, in a new tab (test).
Unconfigured cells don't link (test).
A reviewer compares the cell links with the design and accepts them (visual comparison).

issues.title: Deliver one self-contained file per report
issues.scopeSection:
**In:**
- One HTML file per report, `portfolio.html` and `<StudyID>.html`, with scripts, styles and data inline, requiring no external runtime resources.
- Relative links between reports.
- Data injected into the built template after the build, by a Node injector and by a base R injector that needs no Node or Bun at render time.
- Each report validates its data against a JSON Schema when it loads.
- The portfolio view state carries over to a study report and back, as listed in 27.05.

**Out:**
- Hosting and access control.
- The R package that calls the R injector.

criteria.text: Every report is one HTML file with its scripts, styles and data inline, requiring no external runtime resources. It opens offline from `file://` and under a sub-path.
Reports link to each other with relative URLs.
Data is injected after the build. The base R injector needs no Node or Bun at render time, and the Node and R injectors produce byte-identical files for the same input.
A data document that fails its schema shows an error state, not numbers.

The portfolio view state carries over to a study report and back: the selected view, folded categories in the table and distribution views, grouping and open groups, sorting, cell display, heatmap and palette, study filters, metric-status filters, hidden metrics and the highlighted study. The study report applies the metric-status filters and hidden metrics.
